eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current short-range forecasts from MetService place Wellington’s maximum temperature on Monday, August 3 at 15 °C under southerly flow, with overnight lows near 5 °C.** This aligns closely with the market’s tight clustering around 15–16 °C.  

Wellington’s winter temperatures are highly sensitive to wind direction and the passage of cold fronts. Persistent southerlies or freshening winds off Cook Strait tend to cap daytime highs near or below the seasonal average of ~12–13 °C, while any temporary shift to lighter northerlies or clearer skies can allow readings to reach 16 °C. Recent model runs show modest spread on the exact timing and strength of an approaching front, producing the near-even split between 15 °C and 16 °C implied probabilities.  

El Niño-driven west-to-southwest flow established this winter has kept regional temperatures near or slightly below average, but the two-day lead time means local mesoscale adjustments (cloud cover, wind gusts) will determine whether the peak stays at 15 °C or edges into the low 16 °C range. Updated guidance from MetService or NIWA later today or tomorrow is the next key catalyst that could shift the narrow 44 %–37 % margin.

No significant tropical cyclone or frontal passage is forecast within the 48-hour window, so the primary variables remain radiative heating under clear conditions and the strength of the onshore flow. Updated KMA and global model runs over the next 24 hours will likely tighten the range and move the market-implied odds accordingly.
